skill.name: claude-api
skill.description: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API and Anthropic SDK applications across Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, C#, PHP, and cURL. Includes guidance for Messages API, tool use, streaming, batches, files, prompt caching, and Managed Agents.
skill.summary: Build Claude API and Anthropic SDK integrations with language-specific examples and prompt caching guidance.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: The confirmed findings are mostly expected for an official Claude API skill: examples use network calls, environment-backed credentials, file uploads and downloads, and shell snippets. Many scanner hits are false positives caused by markdown links, inline code, Java builder methods, Go import blocks, and TypeScript template literals. Two contextual issues need author attention: unsafe filename handling in one download example and default unrestricted Managed Agent networking examples.

remediation.issue: Unsafe filename handling in the TypeScript Managed Agents download example.
remediation.suggestion: Save downloads under a fixed output directory and use path.basename plus validation before writing each file.

remediation.issue: Managed Agents setup examples default to unrestricted networking.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer restricted networking in starter examples or add clear production guidance for allowed_hosts and egress review.

remediation.issue: Examples read API keys and GitHub tokens from environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege token scopes, avoid logging secrets, and recommend vaults or secret managers for production deployments.

content.value_statement: Claude API work requires accurate SDK usage, model settings, streaming, caching, and tool patterns. This skill provides language-specific guidance for building reliable Anthropic applications in Codex and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Routes users to Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, C#, PHP, or cURL examples.
Explains Messages API usage for text, images, documents, streaming, and structured outputs.
Provides tool use patterns, including manual loops and SDK tool runner guidance.
Covers prompt caching placement, cache validation, and common cache invalidators.
Documents Managed Agents setup, sessions, environments, events, files, tools, and MCP patterns.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for errors, model selection, batches, files, and long outputs.
limitations: It is specific to Claude and Anthropic SDKs, not provider-neutral AI integrations.
Some model and beta feature notes are cached and may require live documentation checks.
C# coverage excludes Managed Agents because the skill states that support is unavailable.
Examples may need security hardening before production use, especially for files, tokens, and networking.

use_cases.title: Add Claude to an application
use_cases.description: Implement a Claude API request using the official SDK and project language conventions.

use_cases.title: Debug Anthropic SDK behavior
use_cases.description: Resolve errors involving models, streaming, tool calls, structured outputs, files, or rate limits.

use_cases.title: Design a managed agent workflow
use_cases.description: Plan agent setup, sessions, environments, file mounts, event streams, custom tools, and MCP access.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic Claude call
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a basic Claude API request to my project. Detect the language and use the official Anthropic SDK.

prompt_templates.title: Add streaming and errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve reliability for a user-facing response flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add streaming response handling and typed error handling to my existing Claude API integration.

prompt_templates.title: Implement tool use
prompt_templates.scenario: Add controlled function calling or code execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Claude tool use flow with validation, tool results, retries, and clear approval boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Managed Agents system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced agent architecture with sessions and hosted workspaces.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Managed Agents workflow with environment setup, persistent agent IDs, streaming events, files, and MCP access.

output_examples.input: Add Claude API support to a Python service.
output_examples.output: A language-specific implementation plan with SDK setup, environment variable handling, request flow, streaming choice, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: My prompt cache is not being hit.
output_examples.output: A cache audit checklist covering stable prefix order, cache breakpoints, volatile content, token minimums, and usage metrics to inspect.

output_examples.input: Create a Managed Agent for code review.
output_examples.output: A setup and runtime design that separates persistent agent creation from per-run sessions, event streaming, repository mounts, and credential handling.

best_practices: Use official SDKs unless the user explicitly asks for raw HTTP or cURL.
Check live official documentation when cached model or beta feature details may be stale.
Keep credentials in environment variables or vaults and use least-privilege tokens.
anti_patterns: Do not add Anthropic SDK calls to a file that is intentionally provider-neutral or OpenAI-specific.
Do not recreate SDK types, streaming helpers, or error handling that the official SDK already provides.
Do not save generated files or repository resources without path validation and fixed output directories.

faq.question: Does this skill support Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which programming languages are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, C#, PHP, JavaScript through TypeScript examples, and cURL.

faq.question: Can it help with Managed Agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Managed Agents guidance for setup, sessions, environments, events, files, tools, and MCP.

faq.question: Does it fetch current documentation automatically?
faq.answer: No. It points to live sources and instructs the assistant to fetch official documentation when current details are needed.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy examples directly into production?
faq.answer: No. Review examples for token scope, network restrictions, file path handling, retries, logging, and user approval requirements.

faq.question: Does it work for non-Anthropic providers?
faq.answer: No. It is intentionally scoped to Claude API and Anthropic SDK integrations.
